versions.text: Verify that all components, either individually or as part of a subsystem, have passed all safety-related qualification tests (e.g., proof, burst, vibration, containment, over-speed, acceleration, explosive atmosphere, pressure cycling, and temperature cycling as required for airworthy performance). (For Navy and Marine Corps use only, verify external fuel tanks survive without rupture after fragment impact, forced ejection, overpressure following ignition of fuel vapors, and are fire resistant.)

Criterion: Verify that all components, either individually or as part of a subsystem, have passed all safety-related qualification tests as required for airworthy performance. Standard: All fuel system components have been subjected to qualification testing commensurate with their intended operational usage. The following represent typical airworthiness standards: performance for the specified operational envelope, proof, burst, vibration, containment, over-speed, acceleration, explosive atmosphere, pressure cycling, electromagnetic environmental effects, temperature cycling and fluid compatibility. This does not represent a comprehensive and complete list; additional qualification may be needed based upon the operational requirements of the air vehicle system. Method of Compliance: Fuel system components are verified for all specified operating and environmental conditions using analyses, simulator tests, component tests, and ground/flight tests. Components require analysis, component level testing or ground based simulator testing to verify safety. Limited safety of flight testing can be considered to permit initial flight test without fully qualified hardware. Life limits and restrictions are defined as required. Reference: SAE ARP8615

Standard: All components, either individually or as part of the fuel system, have completed and passed qualification testing (e.g., durability). Life limits and restrictions are defined because of qualification testing. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Review of SOF testing documents or qualification test reports to verify ability of the fuel system and subsystem components to operate and perform their intend function, within the installed operating environment.
(2) Review flight and maintenance manuals to verify life limits and procedures are documented due to incomplete qualification test or failures which occurred during qualification testing. Analysis.
  (1) Conduct component SOF and qualification analysis to verify requirements, capabilities, and limitations. Test.
    (1) Lab test: Conduct qualification testing to verify the ability of the fuel system components to perform their intended function and meet specified requirements within the installed operating environment.
    (2) Lab test: As an alternative to Test MoC (1), conduct SOF testing to verify components meet minimum testing requirements in the event full qualification is not achieved before first flight. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
    (3) Lab test: Complete full qualification testing of any components not fully qualified prior to flight test in Test MoC (2) to verify the ability of the fuel system and subsystem components to perform their intended function and meet specified requirements within the installed operating environment.
